generalized_learning.generalized_failure_pattern: A custom structural/data-flow guard may cover one syntax representation while omitting semantically equivalent mutation operators, callable-origin aliases or assignment binding forms, allowing forbidden behavior to bypass an apparently broad policy.
generalized_learning.plausible_wrong_implementation: Patch only the literal escaped operator or binding shape instead of varying operation, callable origin and assignment target shape under mutation controls.

reusable_control.procedure: For a forbidden value flow, vary mutation operator, callable-origin aliasing and declaration-versus-assignment binding while retaining canonical and shadowing allowed controls; mutate each detector to prove the controls fail when coverage is removed.
reusable_control.expected: All forbidden semantic siblings are rejected, allowed controls remain accepted, and documentation names only exercised surfaces.

generalized_learning.prevention_rule: Before implementing a custom structural-flow guard, enumerate semantic equivalence classes across operators, callable origin and assignment/binding targets, then encode at least one discriminant mutation control for each material class.
generalized_learning.detection_rule: Adversarial review must move the same forbidden flow across compound mutation, callable aliases and assignment destructuring and verify that disabling each propagation rule causes a focused control to fail.

transfer_cases.case: Replace a direct concatenation with a semantically equivalent compound assignment on the protected value.
Alias a trusted/taint-producing callable through one or more neutral bindings before invocation.
Move destructuring from declaration syntax to later assignment syntax for the same value flow.

skill_changes.validation: The existing structural-invariant contract is applied with an explicit semantic-equivalence matrix and mutation controls in this delivery.
The audit escape protocol is consumed as a reusable cross-surface control with literal and sibling cases.
